newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries mired in London on weak pre-data demand.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries mired in London on weak pre-data demand.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were slightly weaker in London, as trade slowed to a trickle ahead of producer price data later in the session, traders said.
Many investors have already covered their short positions, leaving little buying interest, although the underlying tone remains positive.
"After the strong move on yesterday's retail sales, a lot of the shorts were already out," said a trader at a European bank in London. "Things have been a little bit quiet today."
The U.S. 30-year long bond was at 98-05, up slightly from 98-04 in Tokyo and 98-02 at the New York close. The September T-bond future was down 2/32 at 111-10 in automated trade.
Analysts and traders said expectations of an imminent rise in U.S. interest rates at the July 1-2 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee had diminished.
"I'm still in the camp which thinks rates will rise, but I'm now in a minority," said Andrew Davies, bond analyst at the London Bond Broking Company here.
U.S. May producer price data were scheduled for release at 1230 GMT. The forecast was for a rise of 0.1 percent on the month, to give a year-on-year rise of 0.9 percent.
"There's a chance the figure will come in higher than the consensus, due to strength in raw material prices," said Davies.
Excluding volatile food and energy prices the rise was forecast at 0.1 percent in May.
U.S. business inventories for April were due out at along with PPI, and the Michigan survey was expected to follow at 1400 GMT.
Analysts said the machinations over European Economic and Monetary Union were continuing to benefit dollar denominated assets.
"What will become of the EMU project is such a tough call that investors can't see which way to jump," said Davies. "They're putting their money into dollars and Swiss francs."
He said short-dated Treasury bills were particularly popular.

The trader at the European bank said the outcome of the Amsterdam summit early next week would be crucial, as a failure to ratify the single currency stability pact could send money flooding across the Atlantic.
December Eurodollar futures were up 0.005 at 93.93. -- Lisa Wilson, International Bonds Unit + 44 171 542 6137
